parsed.headline: Climate Change Authority chair questions economic assessment of Hunter Valley Operations mine extension

pages.text: Matt Kean, chair of the Climate Change Authority, has questioned why the New South Wales Independent Planning Commission did not weigh the economic cost of climate change caused by burning coal from the Hunter Valley Operations mine before approving the project to run until 2045. Speaking in an interview on 2GB radio on Thursday, Kean stated that while the commission acknowledged the project would contribute to climate change, it had not estimated the climate-related economic damage in NSW when weighing local costs and benefits. Kean noted evidence suggesting climate-related disasters could cost Australians at least $73bn a year by 2060. The mine's owners, Yancoal and Glencore, forecast that the project could lead to the release of 809m tonnes of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere once the coal is exported and burned, a figure nearly double Australia’s annual climate pollution. The Independent Planning Commission previously determined that the greenhouse gases from the coal mined near Singleton would affect the people, economy, and environment of the Hunter region, NSW, and the world, but concluded those impacts were outweighed by local benefits such as employment, economic activity, royalties, and taxation revenue. NSW Labor premier Chris Minns applauded the decision, describing it as the right decision that is hugely important for the state economy and responsible for thousands of direct and indirect jobs while producing billions of dollars in royalties. Minns did not mention the development's projected climate impact during the interview.

parsed.headline: Israeli election approaches amid political deadlock and Flydubai midair altercation investigation

pages.text: Israel faces a parliamentary election in less than a month that could determine whether Benjamin Netanyahu remains prime minister. Recent polling indicates a potential deadlock in the Knesset; a Channel 13 poll published last week projected Jewish Israeli parties opposed to Netanyahu to win 52 seats, while Netanyahu’s bloc was projected to win 51, both falling short of the 61-seat majority required. Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party topped the same poll with 22 seats. While Netanyahu’s coalition has been predicted to slip below the majority threshold for over two years, Eisenkot faces challenges to forming a government because he has ruled out coalitions with parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, who are projected to hold 12 seats. The political landscape follows nearly three years of war in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran, and the Hamas attacks of October 7, 2023. On the streets of Jerusalem, citizens remain divided between those pledging support to the prime minister and those seeking change, with some expressing distrust in all political options. On September 29, 2026, Netanyahu released a video statement warning of indications that enemies might attempt attacks ahead of the elections, a claim his opponents dismissed as unevidenced fearmongering.

On September 30, 2026, a Flydubai flight (FZ1073) traveling from Dubai to Tel Aviv was diverted to Tabuk airport in Saudi Arabia following a midair altercation in the cockpit. According to reports, an unnamed co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain, an Indian national identified as Smit Machchhar, and attempted to take control of the aircraft. The plane reportedly plunged more than 17,000 feet during the incident, causing the rudder to be ripped off. Passengers and crew members were able to overpower the attacker and stabilize the plane. Captain Machchhar was reported to be in stable condition in a hospital. The United Arab Emirates’ chief prosecutor, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, has launched an investigation to determine if the incident was linked to terrorist activity, intent, or prior planning. Netanyahu stated that the suspect is being investigated in Saudi Arabia and is expected to be transferred to the UAE. While Netanyahu claimed the co-pilot had undergone 'Islamist radical indoctrination' and suggested potential Iranian involvement, he also noted it was too early to establish a specific motive or confirm Iran's role. The Israeli foreign ministry stated that passengers on the aircraft included citizens from Israel, India, and the UAE.

parsed.headline: GCB Bank sponsors UK-Ghana Trade & Investment Summit to support African growth

pages.text: GCB Bank, Ghana’s largest indigenous bank, has reaffirmed its commitment to supporting trade, investment, and private sector growth across Africa as a main sponsor of the UK-Ghana Trade & Investment Summit 2026. Held in Accra under the theme, “A Decade of Trust, A Future Always On: Scaling the UK-Ghana Growth Partnership,” the summit brought together government officials, business leaders, investors, and development partners from Ghana and the UK to explore commercial collaboration and economic growth opportunities. The summit occurred as Ghana and the UK seek to deepen economic cooperation through increased trade, investment, and private-sector partnerships. According to a statement from GCB, supporting platforms like the summit aligns with the bank's role in enabling businesses to grow, invest, and expand beyond national borders.

During a fireside chat at the summit, Linus Kumi, GCB Bank’s Executive Head of Corporate Banking, discussed Ghana's potential as a gateway to Africa. Kumi stated that Ghana's attractiveness as an investment destination should be measured by the ability of businesses to use the country as a platform for accessing markets across the continent. He noted that unlocking this opportunity requires a connected ecosystem involving financing, logistics, market access, payment infrastructure, and regional trade networks. Kumi identified practical challenges for businesses expanding across borders, including foreign exchange management, payment efficiency, access to working capital, and trade-related risks. He underscored that financial institutions can support cross-border trade through services such as trade finance, guarantees, cash management, foreign exchange services, and working-capital financing.

parsed.headline: CSOs urge Ghanaian government to review offshore gold reconnaissance licences

pages.text: Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) representing fisheries and coastal sectors have called on the Ghanaian government to review offshore gold reconnaissance activities along the country's western continental coast. In an open letter addressed to President John Dramani Mahama dated September 28, 2026, the CSOs expressed concerns regarding the potential implications for fisheries, marine ecosystems, and coastal livelihoods, urging the government to protect biodiversity, food security, human rights, and ocean space. While stating they do not oppose responsible investment or lawful resource exploitation, the groups requested urgent clarification and leadership while the project remains at a stage where such questions can influence its direction. The CSOs noted that GoldCoast Resource Corp. disclosures indicate the company holds 10 offshore reconnaissance licences covering approximately 10,000 square kilometres. This licensed area extends roughly 300 kilometres along the coast between Half-Assini and Winneba and reaches approximately 33 kilometres offshore.

The CSOs stated that published maps suggest portions of the licensed area fall within Ghana’s Inshore Exclusion Zone (IEZ), which extends from the coastline to 12 nautical miles offshore under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Act, 2025 (Act 1146). However, the groups noted that the precise extent of any overlap can only be established once official licence instruments and cadastral coordinates are made public. According to company disclosures, approximately 50,000 line-kilometres of airborne magnetic data have been collected, with detailed work focused on a 500 square-kilometre priority area near the mouth of the Ankobra River. The company's stated forward programme includes marine bathymetric and seismic surveys, followed by bulk seabed sampling and vibro-core drilling. The CSOs raised questions regarding the legal basis for dredging, sampling, and eventual extraction, citing Section 32(3) of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), which they say prohibits holders of reconnaissance licences from drilling or excavating. GoldCoast Resource Corp. has acknowledged that no economic viability or mineral reserves have yet been established.

parsed.headline: Toronto Region Board of Trade urges provincial reform of zoning and building codes

pages.text: The Toronto Region Board of Trade is urging the province of Ontario to amend zoning and building code rules, stating the province is on pace to fall short of a 2022 provincial goal to build at least 1.5 million new homes by 2031. In a report published Thursday, the board asserted that the target is unachievable by the current deadline even if housing production increases over the next five years. According to the board's analysis of budget forecasts, Ontario is projected to fall more than 550,000 homes short of the pace required by 2029. Board president and CEO Giles Gherson described existing zoning and building code rules as out of date and very fragmented across the province. Gherson stated that in Toronto, builders face dozens of different requirements, which he said adds cost and delay to development.

The board noted that even if ambitious reforms were adopted immediately, municipalities would still need to update plans, amend zoning bylaws, align infrastructure investments, service land, and process applications, a process that could take years. The board's report suggests these factors make the 2031 goal unrealistic. Gherson stated that regulatory changes are the key to unlocking new development at a quicker pace, noting that current requirements impact the city's ability to attract and retain a workforce and affect the ability of the next generation to achieve home ownership.

parsed.headline: Trump signs executive order directing U.S. agencies to use the term Super Intelligence

pages.text: President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Sep. 29 titled “Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence,” directing federal agencies to replace the term “artificial intelligence” (AI) with “Super Intelligence” (SI) in official government communications. According to the North Press Agency, the order states that modern AI capabilities have advanced beyond the original description of artificial intelligence, arguing the technology now amplifies human creativity and enables applications in fields such as science and medicine. Trump told reporters that the name had been officially changed to SI, stating, “It’s not artificial, we all agree on that.”

Under the order, federal departments and agencies are required, to the extent permitted by law, to use “Super Intelligence” and “SI” instead of “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI” in official correspondence, public communications, websites, reports, policy documents, and other non-statutory materials. Previously issued regulations and documents are not required to be changed. The order also directs the assistant to the president for science and technology to submit proposed legislation within 60 days for a federal definition of “Super Intelligence” and SI. Trump had previously announced the proposed terminology change during an address to the UN General Assembly on Sep. 22, where he also rejected calls for tighter controls on AI development. In the technology field, the term “superintelligence” generally refers to a hypothetical AI system with cognitive abilities exceeding humans across virtually all areas, a system that has not been achieved.

parsed.headline: Israeli officials investigate whether pilot's stabbing of co-pilot on Israel-bound flight was attempted terror attack

pages.text: Israeli officials are investigating whether an incident on a Flydubai flight from the United Arab Emirates to Israel was an attempted terror attack after a pilot stabbed his co-pilot and appeared to attempt to crash the aircraft, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The plane, carrying 174 people, was forced to make an emergency landing at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz international airport, also known as Tabuk airport, in Saudi Arabia. The two pilots were wounded during the incident, while other passengers remained safe, according to a statement from the airport. The accused pilot is reportedly being questioned in Saudi Arabia. The stabbed pilot has been identified as Captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian national. Netanyahu credited Machchhar with saving the lives of those onboard, stating that despite being seriously injured, the captain resisted the attacker and opened the cockpit door to allow passengers and crew to subdue the individual. The Indian embassy in the United Arab Emirates reported that Machchhar is in good health and recovering well in a hospital in Tabuk. Eyewitnesses reported that the attacker attempted to barricade himself in the cockpit and tried to disable the controls, causing the aircraft to descend 17,000 feet in two minutes. Passenger Yaniv Hayoun recounted hearing screaming and feeling pressure during the dive before forcing entry into the cockpit, where he described finding the attacker at the instrument panel. Another passenger, Miryam Shira Ohayon, told reporters at Tel Aviv airport that a pilot had attempted to carry out a suicide attack on the plane. Machchhar, who joined Flydubai in 2022, had previously worked for SpiceJet and trained in New Zealand.

parsed.headline: Political scientist backs Paul Afoko to lead NPP rebuilding efforts

pages.text: Dr. Kwasi Amakye-Boateng, a Senior Lecturer at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), has endorsed former New Patriotic Party (NPP) National Chairman Awentami Paul Afoko in the race for the party's chairmanship. Speaking on Akoma FM in Kumasi, Dr. Amakye-Boateng stated that Afoko is the candidate best positioned to help rebuild the party by reaching out to disgruntled and former members to bring them back into the fold. He assessed that the other candidates contesting the position do not possess the same capacity to engage aggrieved and breakaway members. According to Dr. Amakye-Boateng, the party's rebuilding process should encompass reconciliation, organizational restructuring, and institutional renewal, and he suggested Afoko's political background and previous experience within the NPP make him suitable to spearhead a new identity for the party. He further noted that the National Chairman role requires a credible and reliable individual with the experience necessary to strengthen confidence in the party. The four candidates contesting the National Chairmanship are John Boadu, Sammy Crabbe, Paul Afoko, and Boakye Agyarko, who have been assigned ballot positions one through four respectively. The NPP is scheduled to hold its national executive elections on October 3, 2026, as part of a reorganization ahead of the 2028 general election.

parsed.headline: Researchers develop ivermectin formulation for children under five

pages.text: Researchers are developing new formulations of the prescription medicine ivermectin to enable its use in children weighing less than 15 kilogrammes, a group currently excluded from ivermectin-based public health programmes due to insufficient safety evidence. The Kumasi Centre for Collaborative Research in Tropical Medicine (KCCR) at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) is leading the IVM-KIDS project, an international effort to expand the drug's use for treating parasitic and worm infections among children under five. While the formulation is reportedly ready for trials, researchers are currently preparing documentation for submission to the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) and ethics committees to seek approvals, with the goal of beginning trials in early 2027. On September 30, 2026, representatives from eight partner organisations met in Accra to coordinate the four-year clinical research programme. The consortium includes researchers, clinicians, pharmaceutical experts, and public health specialists from Ghana, Kenya, Tanzania, the Democratic Republic of Congo, the United Kingdom, Spain, and Switzerland. The IVM-KIDS project is funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe Research and Innovation programme through the Global Health EDCTP3 Joint Undertaking.

parsed.headline: Public safety concerns emerge as key election issue in Toronto despite declining crime data

pages.text: Public safety is becoming a significant consideration for voters ahead of the Oct. 26 election in Toronto, according to polling data. While police data indicates that serious crime is down and the city is broadly getting safer, public opinion suggests residents remain concerned. A survey released earlier this month by Mainstreet Research found that 52 per cent of respondents felt crime and safety were extremely or very important in the election, while almost 70 per cent said they were extremely or very worried about the issue. This disconnect follows a series of high-profile incidents over the past year, including a shooting at the Salsa on St. Clair street festival in July, two incidents at the United States Consulate in downtown Toronto in March and July, and various police-released videos showing car thefts.

Quito Maggi, CEO of Mainstreet Research, suggested that the prevalence of people recording incidents on mobile devices and posting them to social media may exacerbate the perception of violence. Maggi noted that a single incident, such as one on a subway, can be viewed from multiple different angles online.

parsed.headline: Trump dismisses low poll ratings as ‘fake numbers’ in Time interview

pages.text: In a wide-ranging interview with Time magazine, President Donald Trump dismissed low poll ratings as “fake numbers” and deflected responsibility for misleading Americans regarding the duration of the Iran war. According to an Associated Press/NORC Center for Public Affairs Research poll, 31% of people approve of Trump’s handling of his job as president, while 26% of adults approve of the economy under his administration. Trump did not rule out the possibility of declaring a state of emergency before the midterms. 👨‍⚖️

parsed.headline: GoldBod and Kyrgyzstan discuss gold and critical minerals partnerships

pages.text: Kyrgyzstan is exploring the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) model to assist in formalizing its gold trade, strengthening regulation, and attracting investment into its gold and critical-minerals sector. During a courtesy meeting with GoldBod Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi, Kyrgyzstan Foreign Affairs Minister Jeenbek Kulubayev expressed interest in opportunities for technical cooperation, investment, and knowledge-sharing. Mr. Kulubayev stated that Kyrgyzstan has begun reforms to formalize a gold sector that has remained largely informal for approximately 25 years. To facilitate structured technical exchanges and institutional cooperation, Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa proposed a formal framework agreement that would include future engagements with industry experts, entrepreneurs, and investors.

Mr. Gyamfi outlined reforms implemented by GoldBod since its establishment in 2025, which include measures to increase value retained from mineral resources, strengthen controls against smuggling, and formalize Ghana’s domestic gold trade. According to Mr. Gyamfi, gold captured from the artisanal and small-scale mining sector rose to 104 metric tonnes from a previous level of approximately 60 tonnes. He further stated that the sector generated about US$10.8 billion in foreign exchange for Ghana in 2025.

parsed.headline: Syrian government denies reports of meeting with Hezbollah in Türkiye

pages.text: Syria’s Ministry of Information denied reports on Thursday that representatives of the Syrian government held a meeting with Lebanon’s Hezbollah in Türkiye. The ministry’s External Media Directorate stated that the claims were false and that no such meeting took place. This denial follows a report from Reuters, which cited six sources familiar with the discussions, alleging that Syrian government representatives and Hezbollah officials held direct talks in Türkiye last month. According to Reuters, the meeting was facilitated by Turkish security and intelligence agencies and represented the first known direct dialogue between the Syrian government and Hezbollah since the ousting of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad in 2024. The Reuters report indicated that the discussions focused on security concerns, including Syrian accusations that Hezbollah was smuggling weapons through Syrian territory, though the sources stated that no final agreement was reached.
